us4419558.label: US 4419558, background section (resistance welding monitoring/control)
us4419558.note: Gives the squeeze / weld / hold / off sequence.

us5349153.label: US 5349153, background section (spot welding electrode, coated metals)
us5349153.note: I2R at electrode-sheet and sheet-sheet interfaces; highest heat between sheets; forging pressure; hold time and cooling.

nstu-rsw-almg.label: NSTU, resistance spot welding of an Al-5Mg alloy (parameters)
nstu-rsw-almg.note: Heat max at contact interface; copper conductivity and water cooling; zones; expulsion definition. Alloy is aluminium, not steel.

osaka-jwri39-166.label: Osaka Univ. JWRI, nugget formation in multi-sheet stack-ups
osaka-jwri39-166.note: Nugget develops first at the sheet-to-sheet interface; water-cooled copper electrodes.

hirsch-leibovitz-unitrol.label: Hirsch and Leibovitz (Unitrol Electronics), electrode force in resistance welding, conference paper (venue not stated in the document)
hirsch-leibovitz-unitrol.note: Read in full. Low force or early current -> expulsion, heavier indentation, electrode face growth; long weld time can also expel; high force -> shallow, low-ductility nuggets; squeeze time lets force build. Company paper with test data on cold-rolled and galvanized steel. Cites RWMA Resistance Welding Manual 4th ed.

wikipedia-erw.label: Electric resistance welding (Wikipedia)
wikipedia-erw.note: Expulsion leaves a thinner, weaker weld. Tertiary source.

awsforum-126723.label: AWS forum, practitioner discussion on squeeze time
awsforum-126723.note: Practitioner opinion: tighter contact lowers resistance. Not a formal source.

osu-we601-slides.label: Ohio State welding engineering course slides, resistance welding
osu-we601-slides.note: Shows the four-interval cycle and cites AWS Welding Handbook Vol. 2 p. 538 (edition not stated). Handbook not read.

asee-solidification.label: ASEE paper, solidification concepts through organic analogs of welding
asee-solidification.note: Epitaxial growth, growth roughly perpendicular to the pool boundary.

iitkgp-weldzone.label: IIT Kharagpur virtual lab, weld zone evaluation
iitkgp-weldzone.note: Fusion zone, partially melted zone, HAZ definitions.

dtic-ada137272.label: DTIC ADA137272
dtic-ada137272.note: Epitaxial grain growth at the fusion boundary / HAZ interface.

yarmuch-patchett-2007.label: Yarmuch and Patchett, Welding Journal, July 2007, 86(7): 196-s (American Welding Society)
yarmuch-patchett-2007.note: Read in full. Five arc regions; thermionic emission at the tungsten cathode; about 60 to 80 percent of heat at the anode in DCEN GTAW. Paper concerns GTAW of aluminium; cites AWS Welding Handbook Vol. 2 p. 86 and Vol. 3 pp. 37-38.

twi-polarity-faq.label: TWI FAQ: electrode polarity
twi-polarity-faq.note: About two thirds of heat at the anode; tungsten cooled by thermionic emission.

haynes-gtaw.label: Haynes International, GTAW guide
haynes-gtaw.note: DCEN, argon, HF start, pre/post purge, up/down slope.

openwa-gtaw.label: Open WA welding textbook, GTAW equipment

us12343825.label: US 12343825, background section (TIG preflow/postflow/arc start)
us12343825.note: Contact starts can leave tungsten traces.

jmep-sulfur-oxygen.label: J. Mater. Eng. Perform., effect of sulfur and oxygen on weld penetration of austenitic stainless steels

mmtb-stationary-gta.label: Metall. Mater. Trans. B, stationary GTA pool model

oreper-szekely-1984.label: Oreper and Szekely, J. Fluid Mech. 147 (1984) 53-79, heat- and fluid-flow phenomena in weld pools
oreper-szekely-1984.note: Abstract and author list verified. Idealized TIG pool: electromagnetic, buoyancy and surface-tension forces; focused heat flux gives strong electromagnetic flow; surface-tension gradients can reshape the pool.

mendez-graz.label: Conference paper hosted on P. Mendez's page, Univ. of Alberta (Mathematical Modelling of Weld Phenomena 5, 2000); author list not confirmed
mendez-graz.note: Read most of the text; first page with authors was not in the extract. Marangoni dominant under about 200 A; at about 305 A with a deeply depressed pool, gas shear dominates and sulfur has little effect.

toolingu-gmaw251.label: Tooling U-SME, Introduction to GMAW 251
toolingu-gmaw251.note: CV source, DCEP, amperage set by wire feed speed, CTWD = extension + arc length.

ewi-gmaw-basics.label: EWI, GMAW basics: welding current and voltage
ewi-gmaw-basics.note: Constant-voltage source and wire feed speed.

us20200130094.label: US 2020/0130094, background section (starting arc welding)
us20200130094.note: Wire is run in to touch the work to start.

us4079231.label: US 4079231, background section (touchwork MIG)
us4079231.note: High surge current at arc strike.

us6013896.label: US 6013896, background section (GMAW method)
us6013896.note: Short-circuit transfer: current too low to detach the drop by electromagnetic force and weight.

weldguru-transfer.label: WeldGuru, welding transfer modes
weldguru-transfer.note: Globular-to-spray transition in argon-rich gas; attributes detachment to pinch force.

openwa-gmaw.label: Open WA, GMAW operation and techniques
openwa-gmaw.note: Spray: smooth, deeper penetration, ferrous needs at least 80 percent argon.

kim-eagar-1993.label: Kim and Eagar, Analysis of Metal Transfer in Gas Metal Arc Welding, Welding Journal, June 1993, 269-s
kim-eagar-1993.note: Read in full. Transition from globular to spray is gradual, not sharp; pinch-instability theory judged inappropriate for globular and projected spray; static force balance with electromagnetic force fits when electrode taper is accounted for; CO2 and He give repelled transfer; DCEP.

jwjs-30-1.label: Q. J. Jpn. Weld. Soc. 30(1), metal transfer analysis

wang-tsai-2001.label: Wang and Tsai, Metall. Mater. Trans. B, 2001, effects of surface active elements on weld pool flow and penetration in GMAW (doi 10.1007/s11663-001-0035-5)
wang-tsai-2001.note: Abstract and authors verified. Models SPOT GMAW (stationary pool): droplet impact momentum, electromagnetic force, Marangoni effect; sulfur can give inward or outward surface flow.

awshb7-v1.note: User-supplied PDF 'AWS_Welding_Handbook_Volume_1.pdf'; 7th ed., Fundamentals of Welding (1976).
